content: Walk-forward optimization (WFO): re-optimizes parameters on moving in-sample window, tests on immediately-following fresh out-of-sample period -- gold standard since optimal params are not static. Common implementation mistakes: defining WFO parameters AFTER seeing results (must define window type/length/gap before testing any strategy); applying different windows to different candidate strategies (must use same splits for fair comparison); ignoring gap between train and test windows. Anchored WFO = common start point growing window; non-anchored/rolling = fixed-length sliding window. Even WFO strategies fail live when market regime shifts because params were optimized for patterns that won't repeat precisely. Over 90% of academic strategies reportedly fail with real capital due to standard backtesting flaws (in-sample optimization, lookahead bias, black-box ML reliance).
